transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Hill (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (CTO, Delta), Ethan Cole (Platform), Sophie Ramirez (SRE), Tom Li (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect): talk about dedicated pool sizing and VPC peering, discuss KMS and long-term log retention. Customer worried about burst prewarm time and cost during spikes.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm lena from redwood, and with me is marcus our solutions engineer. can you hear ok?
[00:12] Priya Nair: yes, loud and clear. thanks. we've been chatting with your sales team a bit, this is sort of the technical kick off to map out capacity needs.
[00:20] Marcus Hill: great. quick agenda - understand your workload patterns, isolation requirements, burst windows, and any compliance or kms needs. we'll try to map to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private but sounds like Dedicated is top of mind?
[00:33] Ethan Cole: yeah leaning dedicated. we need isolation, and also we have sudden concurrency spikes - marketing campaigns push up QPS by 12x for like 10-20 minute windows.
[00:43] Sophie Ramirez: and we can't have noisy neighbors during those windows, last time cloud tenants caused tail-latency issues.
[00:50] Marcus Hill: understood. can you talk through the typical request size/seq length and what percent are chat vs single-turn generation?
[00:58] Ethan Cole: most are single-turn prompts, avg token out about 150-200, seq length 256ish, but the marketing prompts are richer. concurrency baseline is 200 rps, spike to ~2400 for short bursts.
[01:12] Lena Park: ok that delta looks significant. our reserved pools can be sized with a hotpool prewarm strategy - you can reserve baseline GPUs and have warm nodes that prewarm kv cache to reduce cold-start latencies.
[01:25] Tom Li: about that kv cash, we need to confirm how the cache sits with our VPC. we also need KMS integration for key wrapping, and logs sent to our SIEM with 7-year retention. is that supported?
[01:36] Marcus Hill: yes, we integrate with customer KMS (bring-your-own) via our Private control plane or Dedicated through customer-managed VPC peering. logs can be forwarded via syslog or a secure S3 target; retention is configurable but long retention is something we typically advise pushing to customer's S3/archival layer for cost reasons.
[01:52] Priya Nair: cost is a factor. if we reserve a large pool for 24/7, it could be wasteful outside spikes. what are the economics of reserve + burst?
[02:02] Lena Park: common pattern is commit to a baseline (lower-cost reserved nodes) sized for 2-3x baseline traffic, and enable burst to on-demand capacity for the remaining peak. Redwood's routing policy can fallback to cheaper model variants with slightly lower FP precision for overflow. We'll send a model of cost vs latency in the spreadsheet.
[02:18] Ethan Cole: how fast can you spin up burst nodes? our spikes are short, sometimes 8-12 minutes.
[02:24] Marcus Hill: spin up alone takes a couple mins for node allocation, but the prewarm/hotpool approach keeps a small number already resident and ready. the trick is kv cache: if the model needs a large kv warmup we're working to keep prefix cache warm for hotpool tenants, that reduces tail latencies to near baseline in <30s. if you rely purely on cold on-demand, expect longer 90-120s ramp.
[02:44] Sophie Ramirez: so for 8-minute spikes we need hotpool capacity, otherwise costs blow up.
[02:49] Lena Park: right, that's what most customers do for short, high-concurrency windows. reserve enough hotpool nodes sized for expected concurrency during spike slices, and then let on-demand handle unexpected overflow.
[02:58] Tom Li: what about preemption and eviction? if our nodes are preempted, what's the failover path?
[03:04] Marcus Hill: on Dedicated we avoid preemption; if you're on Dedicated Reserved nodes they're not preemptible. If you're using cloud spot for bursts, Redwood will fallback to a hosted variant (same model family, possibly quantized) to keep requests serving, with a reroute policy.
[03:18] Ethan Cole: and network egress costs? VPC peering to our accounts - any surprise egress charges from redwood or double-billing?
[03:25] Lena Park: peering routes data between your VPC and ours; egress depends on cloud provider billing. Redwood charges for compute/throughput and optional data-handling add-ons, but egress charges are typically passed through as incurred. we can include an egress estimate if you share traffic volumes and region.
[03:39] Priya Nair: we also need audit log immutability for compliance. can logs be signed or have tamper-evident storage?
[03:47] Marcus Hill: we provide auditable log streams and can integrate with your SIEM. for immutability you'd use WORM-enabled S3 buckets on your side; we can push logs to that target. Redwood's control plane also stores operation audit trails if you choose the Private control plane option.
[04:03] Sophie Ramirez: ok good. one more thing: encryption keys - we need HSM-backed KMS, not just standard cloud KMS. is that feasible?
[04:11] Marcus Hill: yes, we support customer-managed KMS including HSM-backed providers, the key wrapping flow requires an initial handshake during deployment - that's typically a Private deployment or Dedicated with customer network setup.
[04:21] Tom Li: great. do you have SOC2 + pen test reports we can share with security?
[04:26] Lena Park: yes, marcus will share SOC2 summary and redacted pentest artifacts. we'll also include a network diagram showing peering and subnets.
[04:34] Ethan Cole: for the benchmark - what sample test should we run? we want realistic patterns including the 12x spike episodes.
[04:41] Marcus Hill: we'll propose a 48h run with a baseline steady-state at your baseline QPS, then scheduled spike windows that emulate your marketing bursts - we can replay traces if you share them. the run will collect tail latency, p50/p95/p99, and token-level cost.
[04:56] Priya Nair: how do you handle fallback when dedicated capacity is saturated? we need predictable latency even under overflow.
[05:02] Lena Park: Redwood's routing supports policy-based fallback: route to another dedicated pool in a different region if reserved capacity is available, or fallback to hosted instances with a compatible model variant. you can set SLO thresholds that trigger fallback automatically.
[05:14] Sophie Ramirez: if we fallback to hosted, what's the data residency impact? that might violate our policy since some customer PII must not leave our VPC.
[05:21] Marcus Hill: good call out. you can tag requests that carry sensitive PII to disallow fallback, or set routing rules that only allow fallback to a Private variant in your VPC. it's a configuration tradeoff: availability vs strict residency.
[05:33] Priya Nair: ok. legal will want to see subprocessor list and egress commitments. we'll need that before procurement.
[05:39] Lena Park: we'll include our subprocessors and proposed contractual language in the packet.
[05:44] Ethan Cole: one more technical detail - how do you manage model versions and rollouts inside Dedicated? we want canary behavior for model updates.
[05:52] Marcus Hill: Dedicated supports model version pinning and canary/A-B rollouts per-route. you can configure weight-based traffic splits and automatic rollback on quality regressions if we detect anomalies against your eval set.
[06:05] Tom Li: auditability on rollouts is important for us - who made the change and when.
[06:10] Marcus Hill: control plane tracks audit events and we can push audit records to your logging target.
[06:15] Lena Park: quick question for sizing - what's your acceptable p99 latency under spike?
[06:19] Ethan Cole: ideally < 800ms, but up to 1.2s might be tolerable for a few minutes. above that we get escalations.
[06:26] Marcus Hill: for 256 seq and typical model family, <800ms p99 during hotpool-backed spikes is achievable. we'll model exact numbers in the benchmark.
[06:34] Priya Nair: on the private/on-prem path - if we later go fully private, what's the migration lift?
[06:40] Lena Park: moving to Private means deploying the control plane inside your network, and you can run the same serving runtime on-prem. there's an operational lift but we provide deployment automation; many customers start Dedicated then migrate to Private when compliance needs mature.
[06:53] Sophie Ramirez: cost/tradeoff? on-prem gives residency but ops cost rises.
[06:58] Marcus Hill: exactly. we can help estimate TCO. for now, Dedicated with VPC peering + strict routing should cover your needs.
[07:06] Priya Nair: can you do a sketch of a recommended baseline configuration?
[07:10] Lena Park: yes - initial recommendation: reserve 4 gpus for baseline (2-3x baseline traffic headroom), maintain a hotpool of 2 prewarmed nodes for quick bursts, and allow on-demand overflow up to another 8 gpus. that'll be our starting model; benchmark will validate.
[07:26] Ethan Cole: sounds reasonable. what's the SLA on dedicated nodes?
[07:30] Lena Park: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for reserved pools; we'll attach SLA table in the packet.
[07:36] Tom Li: about legal/contract: we need assurances on data deletion and certificates for long-retention logs.
[07:42] Lena Park: we'll include our data retention & deletion flow. for logs we can agree on retention lifecycle and certified deletion procedures in contract.
[07:50] Marcus Hill: one more operational note - we'll instrument token-level cost breakdowns and route-level tracing so you can attribute cost to features.
[07:58] Priya Nair: that will be useful. ok, what are the blockers to move forward?
[08:03] Ethan Cole: we need to see pricing and a runbook for VPC peering + KMS handshake, plus SOC2 docs for security.
[08:11] Lena Park: we'll send pricing spreadsheet modeling several reserve/burst mixes, the network runbook and SOC2 docs. propose we run a 48h benchmark once we agree on a small PO or trial commitment.
[08:23] Priya Nair: procurement will need a sample contract too.
[08:26] Lena Park: understood, we'll loop in legal.
[08:29] Sophie Ramirez: timeline - can we get those materials by next week?
[08:33] Marcus Hill: yes, we'll aim to send by 2027-11-16.
[08:38] Priya Nair: good.
[08:40] Lena Park: recap / agreed next steps: redwood to send pricing + SOC2 + network/KMS docs; delta to share traffic traces and retention reqs; schedule benchmark week of 11/22. Anything else?
[08:52] Tom Li: please also include subprocessor list and a sample data deletion clause.
[08:56] Lena Park: will do.

[09:00] (brief pause, folks note calendar invites)

[09:20] Marcus Hill: before we wrap, a quick note about fallback model variants - we can provide a quantized 8-bit variant which has similar latency but slightly different sampling characteristics; we should test for quality regressions as part of the benchmark.
[09:35] Ethan Cole: yes please include that in the run.

[10:00] Lena Park: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with a package and set up the benchmark.
[10:06] Priya Nair: thanks, appreciate it.
[10:10] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: speaker labels are best-effort; there are occasional mis-transcribed tokens (e.g., KV cache -> KV cash).
